2.note: TR adds “and set him over the works of your hands”
The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

8.note: “Behold”, from “ἰδοὺ”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

11.note: The phrase “only born” is from the Greek word “μονογενη”, which is sometimes translated “only begotten” or “one and only”.

12.note: TR adds “or shot with an arrow”
